title: Past the knee, more load delivers less work
summary: Two knees, in different places. Goodput peaks at 64% of rated capacity; throughput peaks later; past both, offering more load delivers less of everything.

steps.title: 150 requests per second: the goodput peak
body: This run offers 150 rps, power-of-two-choices routing. Goodput is 33,068 tok/s, the highest in the sweep, at 93.3% attainment and a first-token p99 of 5,637 ms. Throughput is 35,350 tok/s.
150 rps is 64% of the fleet's rated 235. Below this the fleet is under-used; above it, offering more load buys less delivered value.
steps.look_for: Attainment still above 93% and the goodput/throughput gap still small.

steps.title: Where 150 sits against the rest of the sweep
body: At 30 rps: 7,919 goodput, 98.1% attainment. At 70: 18,127 goodput, 97.0%. At 110: 26,457 goodput, 95.4%. Each step up costs a little attainment for a lot more delivered work.
That trade is still worth it all the way to 150 rps, which is why the peak sits there and not lower.
steps.look_for: The utilization panel: headroom shrinking steadily as offered load climbs toward 150.

steps.title: 190 rps: throughput's own peak, and goodput already falling
body: At 190 rps throughput reaches its peak, 37,976 tok/s, but goodput has already dropped to 31,761 and attainment to 83.3%, with first-token p99 at 8,590 ms.
Between 150 and 190 rps the fleet is doing more work and delivering less value. Two knees, in different places, is the whole finding.
steps.look_for: Throughput still rising while the goodput line has already turned over.

steps.title: 230 rps: both collapse
body: At 230 rps throughput itself falls 20% below its own peak, to 30,175 tok/s. Goodput drops to 18,128 and attainment to 53.2%, with first-token p99 at 38,655 ms.
Offering 53% more load than the goodput optimum (230 vs 150) yields 45% less goodput. Open the A/B view with A = 150 rps and B = 230 rps to see it on the same seed.
steps.look_for: First-token p99 jumping from single-digit seconds to nearly 39 seconds.

steps.title: Admission control is not a refinement here
body: The gap between the peak at 150 rps and the collapse at 230 rps is the entire argument for admission control: it is the difference between the right-hand column of this table and the peak.
No routing policy fixes an offered rate past the knee. The fix is refusing some of the load before it arrives.
steps.look_for: Set arrival rate back to 150 and watch attainment recover without touching the routing policy.
